title: Top-customer signal thresholds and sprint-commit contour
creator: Elena Martinez
description:
Objective: Create a deterministic, signal-driven prioritization framework for top-account feature intake that ties observable escalation signals to a bounded sprint-commit contour and an interruption budget. This ticket defines thresholds, decision rules, stakeholder flows, and the minimum telemetry required to automate routing from Support/Success -> PM triage -> Eng schedule slots.

Background: During Q1 we received several ad-hoc escalations from large customers that disrupted sprint plans. Engineering and Sales pushed for faster delivery while Platform teams raised concerns about long-tail reliability regressions. We need an operationally simple guardrail that preserves runway commitments for existing roadmap items while allowing a measured number of high-impact urgent requests to enter the next-sprint window.

Goal: Deliver a reproducible policy that: (1) quantifies top-account signal thresholds (severity, revenue weight, customer impact score), (2) defines a sprint-commit contour (how many sprint slots can be reallocated per cycle and how far downstream replacements are surfaced), and (3) implements an interruption budget that caps the rate of emergency inserts per account and overall. The intent is to reduce negotiation time, improve predictability for Eng, and provide Sales/CS a transparent escalation path.

Scope: Policy doc + Playbook (Confluence), simple triage dashboard (Pulse) with the computed score and current budget utilization, triage routing rules to update the roadmap intake board, and comms templates for VP-level escalations. This ticket does not include automating ETA calculations in the Customer Console or changing existing SLA contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook published describing thresholds and decision flow
Triage dashboard in Pulse shows calculated score for live escalations and current interruption budget consumption
Playbook includes clear replacement rules: max 2 inserts per sprint across all top-account lanes and a per-account cap of 1 every 3 sprints
PM/Eng/CS sign-off achieved during cross-functional review; Slack thread reference included
One trial run across two upcoming sprints with retrospective notes captured
metrics: Reduction in negotiation time for escalations from 6 business days -> <48 hours
Measure: % of sprints with >0 unplanned high-impact inserts (target <20% after rollout)
Customer satisfaction for escalations (CSAT) maintained at >=4.2/5 for handled requests
Engineering schedule predictability: % of committed roadmap items delivered on time (target +10% over baseline)
rollout_plan: Week 1: Draft thresholds and contour policy; sync with two lead PMs and Eng TPMs
Week 2: Implement read-only dashboard in Pulse ingesting signals from Support and Success; run shadow scoring on last 6 months of escalations
Week 3: Cross-functional review and iterate policy based on shadow-run results
Week 4-5: Pilot policy on two high-velocity accounts; capture process telemetry and CS/Eng feedback
Week 6: Retrospective and adjustments; publish final playbook and train GTM/CS leaders
tradeoffs: Strict caps improve predictability but may frustrate very high-value customers in narrow cases
Shadow scoring requires curated signals — initial false positives/negatives expected until thresholds tuned
Limiting inserts may shift pressure to post-release quickfixes or paid escalation pipelines
Engineering enforcement requires minimal process overhead; avoid heavy workflow automation on first rollout
